blocks.html: 6% of Americans abuse prescribed medications annually, according to the National Center for Drug Abuse and Statistics (NCDAS). Misusing prescriptions occurs when someone takes the medication in a way other than what their Physician directed. Abusing prescriptions does not mean that someone is addicted to the prescription. However, they are at an increased risk of developing an addiction and dependency.

How Do Prescription Drugs Impact the Body?

blocks.html: The different classes of prescription medications will impact our bodies differently. Opioids are often used to treat and manage pain symptoms. These medications bind to opioid receptors in our brain which provide relief from physical symptoms and subsequently can numb or relieve some emotional distress. Depressant medications include benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and sleep medications. These medications affect our Central Nervous System, which can provide relief for symptoms of insomnia, panic attacks, seizures, and anxiety disorders. Examples of stimulant medications include amphetamines and methylphenidate. These medications can be used to increase alertness, attention, and energy. When these medications are abused, individuals can experience paranoia, anger, psychosis, and experience an overdose. What Are the Symptoms of Prescription Drug Withdrawal?

blocks.html: Withdrawal symptoms and the dangers associated with withdrawal vary for the different medications that can be abused.
